issues.observation: Windows native target is available but the service token is NT SERVICE\OrdivonRuntimeR6Candidate. Under limited PowerShell, python --version raised CommandNotFoundException. Our shell script used ErrorActionPreference Continue and eventually returned process exit code 0, so physical Job success did not mean prerequisite success. An independent strict-prerequisite negative-control run set PowerShell ErrorActionPreference=Stop, ran Get-Command python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Stop, and correctly surfaced PROCESS_EXIT_NONZERO exitCode=1 in the same service principal. Thus a consumer script can fail closed today even though Python remains unavailable; no Runtime launcher modification is required to fix this particular false-green shell usage.
